what: Road links of the masterplan inside the red line, survey m (x, y). Made offline for the plan drawing named in plan_svg_bytes; PlanBase draws them with his own roads and paths.
method: Which street runs where: the town's street bands (OpenStreetMap centrelines), used only to find the way. Where the survey (DWG layers YOL_SOSE, YOL_TOPRAK, YOL_BORDUR, YOL_KOPRU) has road lines within 8 m, the link is the road between those lines (61 % of the link length), at most 9 m wide; elsewhere it is the street band, 3 to 6 m wide. Centre and width smoothed over about 8 m. Nothing is drawn where no existing street runs.
gate links (72): every town street that reaches the red line is continued on its existing line to the first road or path of the plan, when that is at most 150 m away and no new bridge is needed.

end links (56): every road, path or bridge end of the plan within 25 m of an existing street is led onto it and along it to the next plan road or path, or to the town street at the red line (at most 150 m, no new bridge).
footbridges (4): where his dotted route crosses the water with no bridge surface drawn, a 3.0 m deck under the route. ASSUMPTION: the 3.0 m width; his drawing gives the bridge only as a line.

joins (4): a road or path end of the plan with no existing street to follow is carried on in its own drawn direction (straight, or turned at most 35 degrees as a curve) until it meets the next road or path, at most 120 m, never through a building or over water; same kind and width as the path it continues (curved ones at most 4 m wide).
routes: his dotted route lines moved to the centre line of the path they run on, where that centre is at most 5 m away, then smoothed over 7 m; elsewhere unchanged.
limits: Positions as good as the street bands (survey kerbs where measured, else carried on). 1 ends of the plan are left as he drew them (water or a building ahead, or no road within 120 m, or a pier into the lake): open_ends (frame m: along the frame from its west end, up).
